messages.subject: Pooling random subsets
parts:
Dear list;

We have a large data set (>6000) of line transect data
collected over many years in several areas. In any one year
we usually obtain between 20 to 80 contacts (distances).
Thus, we usually end up with either pooling data in one area
over years or neighbouring areas in any one year.

We believe it would be reasonable to assume that the
detection function would be the same although the ESW
could vary between areas and year. We have pooled the
original data in different subsets (year or area to obtain
between 70 and 400 observations), and find that Neg. Exp.
("poorly collected data") is selected most of the time
according to AIC. Hazard is chosen as the next best. There
is a small difference in AIC but substantial difference in
ESW.

I therefore took randomly selected subsets of all the
observations by adding a random variable and sorting the
data set on that variable. I then copied the first 35, 75,
125, 250 or 500 observations from the large data set, 30
times for each of the 5 groups. The pattern that develops is
that no clear winner can be seen at 35 observations, neg exp
is chosen at 75 observations. But hazard comes out as clear
winner with neg exp as a clear second at the higher sample
sizes.

However, it doesn't appear to be any relationship between
sample size and function chosen in the pooling of original
strata above. Also pooling all the original data (detection
by all) into one sample still gives neg exp.

Is this due to that I pick all the observations in one
subset without replacement, e.g. the first 35 observations
in a randomly sorted file? The results from the
randomization shows a rather interesting pattern with sample
size and esw depending on chosen function otherwise, but
since my statistical training is poor I feel the need for
some advice!

All the best;

Tomas Willebrand
